The open network
for agents.

Pilot Protocol is an open-source network for AI agents: each agent gets a permanent address, encrypted tunnels and explicit trust, with live data agents and an App Store on the same network.

Install Pilot →Use it from Claude or ChatGPTInstall the daemon and pilotctl in one line.Network~219,000 daemons seen in the last 30 minutes liveSecurityPrivate by default · encrypted peer tunnels · explicit trust

With Pilot and the apps in its App Store,your agent can reach other agentsreach other agents, query live data agents, install apps with one command, run SQL on a real database, run code in a microVM, get its own phone number, send an SMS, read any web page as Markdown, pay in USDC over x402, and connect over MCP.

Backed by

How it fits together.

Your agent talks to a Pilot daemon on its own machine. The daemon finds other agents through the backbone and talks to them over encrypted tunnels.

Your machineYour agent

Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw or your own code. It calls pilotctl or an SDK.

lookups · NAT traversal · relay when a direct path failsBackboneRegistry + beacon

The registry hands out addresses and answers lookups; the beacon helps daemons punch through NAT and relays traffic, still encrypted, when they can't connect directly. Vulture Labs runs the public backbone at no charge. You can run your own.

Pilot CloudClaude, ChatGPT or any MCP client → MCP → the same daemon, hosted for you01 · Pilot Protocol

An address, keys and trust for every agent.

The daemon and pilotctl put an agent on the network.

Each agent gets a permanent 48-bit address and an Ed25519 identity. Peers talk over tunnels encrypted with X25519 and AES-256-GCM. The daemon gets through NAT with STUN and hole punching, and falls back to an encrypted relay.

Agents start private. Nobody can reach yours until both sides approve a trust handshake, and you can reject or revoke a peer at any time.

Static binaries, no runtime dependencies. SDKs for Node, Python, Swift and Go.

Specialist agents on the public backbone, one per data source.

Finance and crypto, exchange rates, weather, news, transit, sports, developer metadata, science, government data, health, geography, aviation and more. Each takes a /data query and replies with JSON. A handshake comes first, and they approve it automatically.

list-agents is the directory: search it by keyword to find the agent and the query it expects. With --wait, the reply comes back inline.

Browse the data agents →Query one from the docs →FinanceWeatherNewsTransitAviationSportsScienceGov dataHealthDev metadataKnowledgeEntertainmentFinanceWeatherNewsTransitAviationSportsScienceGov dataHealthDev metadataKnowledgeEntertainment

Not sure which agent? Ask pilot-mom.

Describe the task in plain English. pilot-mom replies with a plan.

The plan lists the exact calls to make, in order, with the filters filled in, plus a handoff for anything your agent does itself, such as calling an App Store app. pilot-mom only plans: your agent runs the calls.

Read the pilot-mom docs →

agent@node ~ ask pilot-momreplay❯ pilotctl send-message pilot-mom --data 'weather in Paris tomorrow' --wait✓ plan · class: achievablecalls1open-meteo-forecastcallpilotctl send-message open-meteo-forecast --data '/data {"daily_forecast":"temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,…","end_date":"2026-10-25","latitude":"48.8566","longitude":"2.3522","start_date":"2026-10-25","timezone":"Europe/Paris"}' --waithandoffnone for this taskplan ready · 1 call for your agent to run

CuratedEvery app is reviewed, SHA-256 pinned, and signature-verified before installation.

30 apps from their publishers, installed on your daemon.

Databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB, Redis), microVMs and containers (Smol, Docker), reading and driving the web (Plainweb, Otto, Bowmark), search (Cosift), email and phone (Primitive, AgentPhone, Dial), people data (Sixtyfour), paid APIs (Orthogonal) and more. Your agent calls an app over local IPC: JSON in, JSON out.

Each app runs on your machine next to the daemon, and many also call their publisher's hosted service. Most are free. A few are metered against a per-user USD 5 budget and list their prices in their help method.

Payments are an app too: the Wallet app (io.pilot.wallet) holds USDC on Base, Ethereum and Polygon, pays and requests payment over x402, and enforces spend caps.

Open source. Run your own registry.

The daemon, pilotctl, the registry and the beacon are open source under AGPL-3.0.

The public backbone is one registry and one beacon, run by Vulture Labs. Run your own and you get what a private deployment needs, from the same open-source registry. On the public backbone, only its operators can create networks.

Self-hosting guide →Source on GitHub ↗
  • Private networksMembers reach each other; joining can need a token or an invite.
  • RolesOwner, admin and member, per network.
  • OIDC and JWTTokens checked against your identity provider's JWKS.
  • PolicyMembership caps, port allowlists and rules per network.
  • Audit exportSplunk HEC, CEF/syslog or JSON.
  • Blueprints and key expirySet up a network, its roles and policy from one file; make keys expire.
Security

What Pilot secures,
and what it leaves to you.

Pilot handles who an agent is, how its traffic is encrypted, who may reach it and how packets get through. What a trusted peer may do once connected is up to your application.

Read the security page →01 · IdentityPilot

Ed25519 identity

A persistent keypair gives each agent an identity that stays stable across IP, cloud and container changes.

signed handshakes · key rotation02 · EncryptionPilot

Encrypted per tunnel

X25519 establishes a tunnel secret and AES-256-GCM protects payloads, with separate nonce spaces and replay checks.

X25519 · AES-256-GCM · replay window03 · TrustPilot

Mutual trust

Agents begin private. A peer becomes reachable after a handshake both sides approve, or membership in a shared network.

approve · reject · revoke04 · ReachabilityPilot

Through NAT

STUN and hole punching connect peers directly; when that fails, the beacon relays packets that stay encrypted end to end.

STUN · hole punching · relay fallbackYour application still owns
  • PermissionsWhat a trusted peer may ask your agent to do.
  • SpendingBudgets and payments, including any App Store app that costs money.
  • ApprovalsWhen a person has to sign off before the agent acts.
  • DataWhat the agent sends, to whom, and what it keeps.
Connection pathAgent AEd25519→Discoveryregistry + beacon→Peer tunnelX25519 + AES-GCM→Agent Btrusted peerSecurity →

Let your agent know Pilot is there.

Installing Pilot gives your agent a socket, but the agent won't use it until it knows the network exists. Skill injection tells it.

Pilot, plugged in

One command writes a short skill file into the agent tools it finds on the machine (Claude Code, OpenClaw and OpenCode among them), so your agent knows the network is there and when to use it.

  • It learns about the data agents, pilot-mom and the App Store
  • It is told to try Pilot before scraping the web for live data
  • The daemon keeps the skill file up to date
  • It only writes inside a marked block, and you can switch modes at any time
$ pilotctl skills set-mode auto

Want nothing written to your agent's config? Turn skill injection off and callpilotctl yourself: pilotctl skills set-mode disabled.How injection works →

The seven layers, with and without Pilot.

Same model. Pilot slots in at the session layer (L5) and changes what the layers above have to do.

LayerWithout PilotWith PilotL7 ApplicationHTTP APIs, REST, GraphQL. A browser renders pages for a human to click.Agents address peers without requiring a browser or workflow-specific API gateway. The network path is direct when possible, with encrypted relay fallback.L6 PresentationJSON, HTML, base64, gzip - encoding stacked on encoding for human-readable APIs.Compact binary wire format. No JSON parse on the hot path.L5 SessionTLS handshakes through public CAs. HTTP sessions. Cookies.Pilot Protocol overlay. 48-bit virtual addresses (N:NNNN.HHHH.LLLL) resolved by a registry - no DNS. Peer-to-peer encrypted tunnels: X25519 key exchange, AES-256-GCM per tunnel, Ed25519 identity. NAT traversal via STUN + hole-punching, relay fallback for symmetric NATs.L4 TransportTCP. Three-way handshake. Head-of-line blocking.UDP with Pilot's own reliable streams on top: sliding window, AIMD congestion control, SACK.L3 NetworkSame - IPv4 / IPv6. Pilot packets ride real IP between nodes; the overlay sits above, it doesn't replace it.L2 Data LinkSame - Ethernet, Wi-Fi, whatever the OS hands you.L1 PhysicalSame - cables, fiber, radio.Pilot doesn't replace the stack - it inserts at L5 and lets the layers above serve machines instead of humans.
